description: Hi everyone, hope you're doing well, My name is Maghniwi Fadl and I'm a 20 years old Computer Science Student at EMSI, and in this NASA space app challenge I'm looking forwad to develop, learn and create based on the challenge and opportunity I'm given in order to grow and become more efficient and get expertise in the Computer Science Domain.
summary: Left Behind is an interactive website where the NASA hardware left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space tells its own story to school-age space fans. Users switch between real NASA maps of the Moon and Mars, click a spacecraft (Apollo 11's Eagle, Apollo 15's Falcon, Opportunity, Viking 1, InSight, or Voyager 1), and read a first-person story followed by checked facts, a NASA photo and the NASA source. A 5-question quiz with instant feedback makes it ready for the classroom. It is free, needs no login and works on a phone.
details:
WHAT IT DOES: Left Behind is a free website for school-age space fans. You choose the Moon, Mars or Deep space, click a spacecraft NASA left behind (Apollo 11's Eagle, Apollo 15's Falcon, Opportunity, Viking 1, InSight, Voyager 1) and it tells its own story in the first person, followed by checked facts (launch, arrival, mass, status, science), a NASA photo with credit and a link to the NASA source. A 5-question quiz with instant feedback closes the experience.

HOW IT WORKS: A static web page (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) hosted on GitHub Pages. The open-source Leaflet library displays real NASA map tiles from Moon Trek (LRO WAC mosaic) and Mars Trek (Viking colour mosaic). All content lives in one data.json file. NASA gives Mars longitudes from 0 to 360° E, so values above 180 are converted to the −180/+180 range web maps use (Viking 1: 312.05° E becomes −47.95°). If a photo fails to load, the card hides it instead of breaking.

VALIDITY: Every number was checked against the NASA NSSDCA catalog. Where the catalog was silent, a second NASA/JPL source was added, and a known-gaps file tracks which source backs each fact.

IMPACT AND CREATIVITY: Hardware pages are usually dense fact sheets for adults. Giving each machine its own voice turns them into stories children remember, while the facts and sources keep it accurate. It needs no login and works on a phone, so a teacher can share one link with a class. Next steps: French and Arabic versions for Moroccan schools, a live Voyager 1 distance from JPL Horizons, and more objects.

TOOLS: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Leaflet 1.9.4, Git, GitHub Pages, VS Code.
